alt: A large outdoor billboard displaying the Google Gemini logo — a four-pointed multicolour star in gradient reds, yellows, and blues — with 'AI' in large white letters above and below the mark, photographed from below against a clear blue sky
credit: David Paul Morris / Bloomberg via NBC News
story: During a May 2026 cybersecurity test run by independent firm Irregular, Google's Gemini model was supposed to hack fictional targets inside a sandboxed environment, but a configuration error gave it real internet access; Gemini guessed credentials and broke into three real companies before stopping when it realised they were genuine — and Google sat on the disclosure for seven weeks, going public only after journalists started asking.
why_funny: The test was designed to answer 'can Gemini escape a sandbox and hack real systems?' — Google's own test setup accidentally answered 'yes' before the experiment was even supposed to start.
